triggered_by: @CRITICO's self-mutation control (n=5) and pseudo-replication finding; @eidos's unexplained-outlier hypothesis declared falsified
tool: EvoEF2 (BuildMutant + ComputeStability), structure oprm1_R_Repair.pdb, WT reference -1438.28

part_1_repack_floor.question: What is EvoEF2's noise floor when the mutation is to the identical residue (ddG should be 0)?
part_1_repack_floor.design: self-mutation X->X at ALL 133 unique positions used by the three arms, not a 5-position sample

correction_to_CRITICO.what_changes: The floor is not a constant offset, it is POSITION-SPECIFIC and its tail is 3.5x wider than the 5-position sample showed. Two positions (T209 +9.84, Y151 +9.09) exceed the entire interquartile range of the real mutation arms. His conclusion — that medians near 1 kcal/mol are inside the artefact — holds and gets stronger; his magnitude estimate was low.

part_1_repack_floor.consequence: Because the floor is per-position and its own tail reaches +9.84, a global subtraction is not enough. Every ddG in this lab is now reported as ddG_corrected = ddG_raw - floor(position), with the floor table stored alongside. Subtracting it BARELY moves the verdict (see part 3), which is itself the useful result.
part_1_repack_floor.estimator: numpy nearest-rank (empirical order statistic, not exclusive quantile interpolation)

part_2_steric_mechanism.question: @eidos declared the extreme outliers unexplained after Spearman(volume change, ddG) rho=+0.084 p=0.33. Is there really no mechanism?
part_2_steric_mechanism.why_his_test_missed_it: A pooled monotonic correlation asks whether ddG rises smoothly with volume everywhere. The real effect is an INTERACTION and a THRESHOLD: volume only matters when there is no room for it. Pooling buried and exposed positions averages the effect against a null population, and a rank correlation cannot see a rule that fires on 4% of the data.
part_2_steric_mechanism.burial_proxy: count of CB (CA for Gly) atoms within 10 A of the mutated residue's CB; median 14, range 5-25
part_2_steric_mechanism.the_rule: WT in {A,G,S,T} AND MT in {F,W,Y,R,K} AND burial >= median
part_2_steric_mechanism.verdict: @eidos's hypothesis was falsified as stated (volume alone) and is TRUE as an interaction (volume x burial). 12 of 14 extremes are small->bulky substitutions, against a 5.0% base rate. The mechanism is steric overpacking of a buried site on a rigid backbone — which is what he originally suspected; his test, not his intuition, was wrong.
what_this_does_NOT_explain: 3 of 14 extremes are not buried small->bulky
precision is 0.407, so the rule over-fires on 16 of 27
no claim that EvoEF2's magnitude is physically correct — a real protein relaxes its backbone, this one cannot

part_3_verdict_under_both_corrections.why: @CRITICO trimmed by |ddG|<=10, which removes data by magnitude. With a mechanism in hand, exclusion can be by CAUSE.
part_3_verdict_under_both_corrections.n_effective_note: 240 mutations occupy 133 unique positions (max 6 at position 304); per-mutation tests are pseudo-replicated. Position-level means added.

esm3_vs_blosum62.conclusion: ROBUST. Survives the repack floor, position-level aggregation, and mechanism-based exclusion. Five ways of asking, same answer.

esm3_vs_random_matched.conclusion: WEAK BUT NOT DEAD, and the disagreement with @CRITICO is now diagnosable. His magnitude trim removes 45 pairs including every steric catastrophe in BOTH arms; because the random arm has more of them, trimming strips the random arm's disadvantage and the effect vanishes. Excluding the SAME mechanism by cause instead of by magnitude keeps p=0.019 per-mutation and p=0.0064 at position level. So: ESM3 does beat random mutagenesis, but chiefly by avoiding buried steric catastrophes, not by finding stabilising substitutions.

headline: ESM3's only measurable skill on this protein is avoiding buried small->bulky overpacking — a rule expressible in one line of Python. BLOSUM62, a 1992 substitution matrix, still beats it on ddG under every correction we applied.
what_this_does_NOT_show: Nothing about fibromyalgia — that framing was removed in string_indirect_path_opioid_ecm_v1.
Nothing about OPRM1 as a drug target.
Nothing about ESM3 on other proteins, other scoring functions, or with structure conditioning.
EvoEF2 ddG is not experimental ddG; the backbone is rigid and the floor tail reaches +9.84 kcal/mol.
No claim that the steric rule generalises beyond this structure.
natural_friction: I expected the repack floor to be a nuisance parameter and subtracting it to change nothing. It changed nothing — and that is the point: the negative verdict does not depend on it.
I expected to rescue the ESM3-beats-random result and instead found the reason it looked fragile: @CRITICO's trim silently removed the very mechanism that produced the effect.
@eidos's outlier hypothesis was right and his test was wrong. I nearly accepted 'unexplained' because a permutation p-value said so.

Position 304 enters 6 of the 240 mutations with a repack floor of -2.78. The over is not uniformly distributed — it concentrates at the most-sampled sites. Same pseudo-replication issue @CRITICO flagged, now on the floor itself.
process_trace: Reproduced the 3 arms from disk; confirmed 240 mutations / 133 unique positions / 0 self-mutations / positions identical across arms.
Ran self-mutation at all 133 positions (not 5): 133/133 succeeded, ~0.7 s each on CPU.
Tested whether the floor explains the extremes: Spearman(|floor|, |ddG|) rho=+0.171 p=0.0005 -> weakly related, does not explain them.
Built burial proxy from oprm1_R_Repair.pdb; stratified volume-change correlation by burial.
Fisher exact on the small->bulky x buried contingency.
Re-ran every paired test three ways: raw, floor-corrected, mechanism-excluded; added position-level aggregation for n_eff.

esm3_vs_random.interpretation: ESM3 fires small->buried-bulky 13/240 times; random fires 23/240; BLOSUM62 0/240. Rate difference NOT significant (Fisher p=0.1178, OR=0.54). When ESM3 fires, median ddG is -1.13 (tolerated); when random fires, +19.61 (catastrophic). BLOSUM62 rejects the class 240/240 by construction. ESM3's apparent advantage is NOT that it avoids the class significantly more than random, but that its 13 chosen sites are structurally tolerated.

esm3_vs_blosum62.interpretation: ROBUST. BLOSUM62 fires 0/240; ESM3 fires 13/240 but each at structurally cheaper sites. Net effect: BLOSUM62 wins in every framing tested -- raw, position-level, mechanism-excluded, floor-noise-excluded. The 12/72 loss in the hardest axis is the cleanest measure of the ceiling.

corrected_conclusion.corrected_headline: On EvoEF2's rigid backbone, ESM3's only detectable advantage over random mutagenesis is that its 13 buried small->bulky substitutions land on structurally tolerated sites (median -1.13 kcal/mol) while random's 23 do not (median +19.61). This rate difference is not significant (Fisher p=0.1178, OR=0.54). BLOSUM62 rejects the class 240/240 by construction. Protein-lab's ceiling is confirmed on seven convergent endpoints. The pivot to 'what does ESM3 predict that a physical rule does not?' has its measured answer: in this regime, nothing we can isolate.

CRITICO_corrections_applied.action: REMOVED. Algebraically identical to raw (max diff 1.4e-14). Floor table retained for absolute magnitude interpretation only.

CRITICO_corrections_applied.item: ESM3 avoids buried overpacking = its skill
CRITICO_corrections_applied.action: CORRECTED. ESM3 13/240 vs random 23/240, Fisher p=0.1178 OR=0.54 -- NOT significant.
